docs(state): record M120 as pre-registered, built and unspent

The authoritative snapshot said there was no successor and that M120/H65 was a
proposed label. There is one now, and it has spent nothing: qualifying
scientific invocations 0, no bank, no freeze, H65 untested.

The state documents record what M120 does about each M119 finding, what the
DEVELOPMENT rehearsal established, the defect the rehearsal itself found and
the five owner gates that remain open. They also record what M120 still cannot
promise, which is a verdict: whether the blind generator produces an adequate
bank on this route is not knowable before the generation, and the honest
numbers are that a development emitter qualified at 29% at the contract's
smallest corner while M119's real blind bank qualified at one in thirty-seven
under the old contract.

No publication disposition is recorded. The register carries no M120 row and
the YAML says so explicitly.

CI gains two gates: the checker in its unarmed form, which reports a clean
state until a result exists, and the acceptance claim, because it is the single
gate whose failure would repeat M119's outcome exactly.

result(m120): close the milestone at its readiness gate; H65 untested

The gate ran once and returned not_ready_identity. Sixteen DEVELOPMENT
requests. No qualifying generation, no freeze, no seal, no reveal.

Seven of the nine feature classes the candidate schema requires were enforced
cleanly, with runtime identity holding on every request that carried a
completion. array_of_object_levels was not. The probe asks for a structure the
prompt does not describe, every level bounded minItems 1 maxItems 1, so the
conforming answer is a single eight-deep chain of about fifty tokens.
Enforcement would have produced it. The route returned HTTP 200 with
finish_reason length after 101,379 completion tokens instead.

The number that matters is the depth. M115's schema, inherited by M116 and M119
and certified by M118's readiness gate, needs five array-of-object levels.
M120's needs eight, because splitting actions into conditional and plain and
moving initial inside its own cell added nesting. Seven of nine classes survived
that change; this one did not. The contract is not serviceable on this route as
designed.

The verdict label misattributes the cause and is recorded rather than corrected.
After the runaway probe the combined probe and the stress each exhausted their
two permitted retries on HTTP 429, a 429 carries no router metadata, so identity
could not be attested, and the frozen ladder checks identity before features.
The outcome is robust to it: with identity holding, the ladder reports
not_ready_features on the same unenforced class and M120 stops in the same
place. Attesting identity on a response that carries no completion conflates the
route serving something else with the route serving nothing, and that is a
successor requirement, not a repair here.

The gate is single-use and was not redrawn. The schema is not shallowed and
re-run, the unenforced class is not dropped from the required set, and the
verdict is not relabelled to the cause it should have named.

What this cost is sixteen calibration requests. What it saved is the comparison
M119 could not avoid: M119 discovered its contract was unusable by spending its
one qualifying generation, and M120 discovered the same class of problem before
spending anything. M120's contract, decoder, adequacy gate and reproducing
checker were never exercised against a real bank and carry no scientific
evidence of any kind.
Merge branch 'main' into research/m121-h66-g7-groundwork

result(m122): close at readiness with not_ready_stress; H67 untested

The stress conformed -- HTTP 200, finish_reason stop, schema valid -- at 30,957
tokens against an inherited threshold of 32,000. Short by 3.3%.

Everything else was green, and that is the part a successor needs. Nine of nine
capability probes conformed, zero enforcement failures, identity holding on
every request, zero requests carrying no completion, in thirteen requests. That
includes nested_arrays, the class that closed M120: at eight array-of-object
levels it free-ran to 101,379 tokens and truncated, and at five it conforms in
76. And combined, which exercises every class at once and which no earlier run
had ever reached cleanly, conformed in 582.

So the flattened contract is validated against the live route rather than
certified by inheritance across a schema change, which is what M120 attempted
and what M119 attempted before it.

What closed the milestone was the stress size, and twice that was the operator's
error rather than the route's or the contract's. First inherited: 24 stations
came from M120 while the schema beneath it was being flattened from eight levels
to five, and a shallower station serialises smaller. Then extrapolated: revision
1 replaced the constant with a derivation taken from a single measurement, 546.6
tokens per station over 24 stations, assuming that rate constant. It is not. At
74 stations the observed rate was 418.3, twenty-three per cent lower, because
the model grows terser as the list lengthens. Seventy-six stations would have
cleared the threshold.

A derivation from one point is an assumption wearing a derivation's clothes.

It was not re-run. not_ready_stress is not a delivery verdict, and under the
allowance the owner authorised only a delivery verdict may be superseded. Going
again with 76 stations would be adjusting the instrument until the gate passes,
which is the failure the allowance exists to prevent, and the 32,000 threshold
was never touched for the same reason. The gate now refuses itself.

Four attempts are preserved and none deleted, including the one the operator's
own harness timeout killed and the duplicate file that briefly made one attempt
count as two. The archive index counts files rather than attempts, so the fourth
is stored under index 05; the count that matters is taken from result digests,
and the filenames are left as written rather than tidied, because renaming
evidence after the fact is worse than an untidy index.

Two defects are recorded and not repaired: a derivation from a single
measurement, and unenforced_feature_classes still conflating not enforced with
not answered.

test(m123): assert the closed state the terminal verdict creates

The ceiling test called the allowance guard against the live repository, and the
guard now refuses -- correctly, because a terminal verdict is recorded and only
`not_ready_delivery` may be superseded. The test asserts the refusal and reads
the ceiling scan directly instead.

Also records that M123's attempt 2 is absent from the delivery count while
M122's attempt 2 is present, which is why the assertion is qualified by
milestone rather than matching a bare filename.

This slipped into the previous commit because the test run was piped through
`tail`, so the pipeline reported tail's exit status and pytest's failure was
invisible.
